units.text: The Compose testing page's setup section says to add the following dependencies to the `build.gradle` file of the module containing your UI tests:

quotes.quote: First, add the following dependencies to the build.gradle file of the module containing your UI tests:

// Test rules and transitive dependencies: androidTestImplementation("androidx.compose.ui:ui-test-junit4:$compose_version") // Needed for createComposeRule(), but not for createAndroidComposeRule<YourActivity>(): debugImplementation("androidx.compose.ui:ui-test-manifest:$compose_version")

units.text: The Robolectric Getting Started page says to start by adding the following to your module's `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts` file:

quotes.quote: Start by adding the following to your module's build.gradle/build.gradle.kts file:
android { testOptions { unitTests { isIncludeAndroidResources = true } } } dependencies { testImplementation("junit:junit:4.13.2") testImplementation("org.robolectric:robolectric:4.18") }

units.text: Compose test v2 APIs use `ComposeUiTestConfig` to customize the test environment. This configuration object consolidates environmental related APIs like `effectContext`, `runTestContext`, and `testTimeout` into a single object.

quotes.quote: Compose test v2 APIs use ComposeUiTestConfig to customize the test environment.
This configuration object consolidates environmental related APIs like

val testConfig = ComposeUiTestConfig( effectContext = EmptyCoroutineContext, runTestContext = EmptyCoroutineContext, testTimeout = 30.seconds ) @get:Rule val rule = createComposeRule(config = testConfig) // OR runComposeUiTest(config = testConfig) {}

units.text: Compose test v2 APIs enforce `InputMode.Touch` by default at the start of each test to ensure determinism and prevent input mode state from leaking between tests. Tests can fail during migration if they rely on non-touch input modes configured through instrumentation APIs before the test starts. To resolve this, specify the required input mode in `ComposeUiTestConfig`:

quotes.quote: Compose test v2 APIs enforce InputMode.Touch) by default at the start of each test to ensure determinism and prevent input mode state from leaking between tests.
Tests can fail during migration if they rely on non-touch input modes configured through instrumentation APIs before the test starts.
To resolve this, specify the required input mode in ComposeUiTestConfig:
class FocusTest { @get:Rule val rule = createComposeRule( config = ComposeUiTestConfig(inputMode = InputMode.Keyboard) ) @Test fun testFocus() {} }

units.text: When running tests on Java 17 or higher, the JVM requires `--add-opens` flags so that Robolectric can access internal OpenJDK classes and APIs (java.lang, java.io, jdk.internal.access, etc.). Add the following `jvmArgs` to your unit test configuration in `build.gradle` / `build.gradle.kts`:

quotes.quote: When running tests on Java 17 or higher, the JVM requires --add-opens flags so that Robolectric can access internal OpenJDK classes and APIs (java.lang, java.io, jdk.internal.access, etc.). Add the following jvmArgs to your unit test configuration in build.gradle / build.gradle.kts:

android { testOptions { unitTests.all { it.jvmArgs( "--add-opens=java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.io=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.net=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.security=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.text=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/jdk.internal.access=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.desktop/java.awt.font=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api=ALL-UNNAMED", ) } } }

units.text: Several aspects of Robolectric's behavior can be configured at runtime, using either `@Config` annotations for class- or method-level configuration, or `robolectric.properties` files for package-level configuration.

quotes.quote: Several aspects of Robolectric's behavior can be configured at runtime, using either @Config annotations for class- or method-level configuration, or robolectric.properties files for package-level configuration.

units.text: To configure Robolectric for a single test class or method, use the `@Config` annotation on the desired class or method. Annotations applied on methods take precedence over the ones at the class level.

quotes.quote: To configure Robolectric for a single test class or method, use the @Config annotation on the desired class or method. Annotations applied on methods take precedence over the ones at the class level.

units.text: Base classes are also searched for annotations. So if you find yourself specifying the same values on a large number of tests, you can create a base class and move your `@Config` annotation to that class.

quotes.quote: Base classes are also searched for annotations. So if you find yourself specifying the same values on a large number of tests, you can create a base class and move your @Config annotation to that class.
@Config( sdk = Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU, shadows = [ShadowFoo::class, ShadowBar::class] ) class SandwichTest

units.text: To configure all Robolectric tests within a package or group of packages, create a file named `robolectric.properties` in the appropriate package. Generally, this file would be placed within the appropriate package directory under `src/test/resources` in your project tree. Robolectric will search for properties files up the hierarchy of packages (including the unnamed default package at the top level), with values in deeper packages overriding values in more shallow packages. When test classes or methods have `@Config` annotations, those override any config from properties files.

quotes.quote: To configure all Robolectric tests within a package or group of packages, create a file named robolectric.properties in the appropriate package. Generally, this file would be placed within the appropriate package directory under src/test/resources in your project tree. Robolectric will search for properties files up the hierarchy of packages (including the unnamed default package at the top level), with values in deeper packages overriding values in more shallow packages. When test classes or methods have @Config annotations, those override any config from properties files.

units.text:
# src/test/resources/com/mycompany/app/robolectric.properties
sdk=33
shadows=com.mycompany.ShadowFoo,com.mycompany.ShadowBar

quotes.quote: src/test/resources/com/mycompany/app/robolectric.propertiessdk=33 shadows=com.mycompany.ShadowFoo,com.mycompany.ShadowBar

units.text: If you wish to change the default for any configurable value for all your tests, you can provide a `GlobalConfigProvider` service implementation.

quotes.quote: If you wish to change the default for any configurable value for all your tests, you can provide a GlobalConfigProvider service implementation.

units.text: By default, Robolectric will run your code against the `targetSdk` specified in your module's `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts` or `AndroidManifest.xml` file. If you want to test your code under a different SDK, you can specify the desired SDK(s) using the `sdk`, `minSdk` and `maxSdk` config properties:

quotes.quote: By default, Robolectric will run your code against the targetSdk specified in your module's build.gradle/build.gradle.kts or AndroidManifest.xml file. If you want to test your code under a different SDK, you can specify the desired SDK(s) using the sdk, minSdk and maxSdk config properties:

@Config(sdk = [TIRAMISU, UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE]) class SandwichTest { @Test fun getSandwich_shouldReturnHamSandwich() { // will run on TIRAMISU and UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE } @Test @Config(sdk = TIRAMISU) fun onTiramisu_getSandwich_shouldReturnChocolateWaferSandwich() { // will run on TIRAMISU } @Test @Config(minSdk = UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE) fun fromUpsideDownCakeOn_getSandwich_shouldReturnTunaSandwich() { // will run on UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE, VANILLA_ICE_CREAM, etc. } }

units.text: Note that `sdk` and `minSdk`/`maxSdk` may not be specified in the same `@Config` annotation or file; however, `minSdk` and `maxSdk` may be specified together. If any of them is present, they override any SDK specification from a less-specific configuration location.

quotes.quote: Note that sdk and minSdk/maxSdk may not be specified in the same @Config annotation or file; however, minSdk and maxSdk may be specified together. If any of them is present, they override any SDK specification from a less-specific configuration location.

units.text: Robolectric will attempt to create an instance of your `Application` class as specified in the AndroidManifest. If you want to provide a custom implementation, you can specify it by setting:

quotes.quote: Robolectric will attempt to create an instance of your Application class as specified in the AndroidManifest. If you want to provide a custom implementation, you can
@Config(application = CustomApplication::class) class SandwichTest { @Test @Config(application = CustomApplicationOverride::class) fun getSandwich_shouldReturnHamSandwich() { } }

units.text: You can explicitly configure the set of resource qualifiers in effect for a test:

quotes.quote: You can explicitly configure the set of resource qualifiers in effect for a test:
class SandwichTest { @Test @Config(qualifiers = "fr-xlarge") fun getSandwichName() { assertThat(sandwich.name).isEqualTo("Grande Croque Monégasque") } }
